Two quick, high-level asks so we can loop Legal: 1) We need clarity that Navitas owns the output generated by our customers and can use that output for our product features (we are productizing LLM responses). 2) We do not want Redwood to re-train models on our customer content or use our logs for general model improvements.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on output assignment + any standard language around a training opt-out? If you have a suggested carveout (e.g., endpoint-specific, time-limited telemetry), that would help speed Legal review.

Alex — appreciate the clear asks and the doc. Looping in Laura (legal) and Monica (CS) so we can give a consolidated response and propose concrete redlines. Quick signal from me: Redwood generally supports customer ownership of outputs (we aim to avoid surprise claims), but we have standard telemetry and safety signals we collect to maintain the service. Laura / Monica — below are the three things Navitas called out; can you propose redlines or options we can send back?

1) Output ownership / assignment to Navitas for customer-generated outputs used in product features.
2) No training on customer content / an explicit training opt-out.
3) Telemetry/telemetry retention and what Redwood may use for service improvements.

Goal: offer a tight, operationally feasible carveout rather than a blanket "no use" that breaks monitoring. Preferably give them two options (conservative and standard).

Alex / team — thanks, we reviewed the v3 Order Form and Navitas note. Below are proposed positions and suggested redline snippets. I kept the language short to make it easy for your counsel to cut-and-paste into the Order Form or MSA exhibit.

1) Output ownership: Proposed: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and in Outputs produced solely from Customer Content under this Agreement. Redwood hereby assigns to Customer, to the extent permitted by applicable law and subject to third-party rights, all of Redwood's rights in such Outputs."
Rationale: gives Navitas explicit assignment while preserving any third-party constraints. Where productization involves combining Redwood-generated outputs with Redwood models (e.g., templates), we should add a limited license back to Redwood for telemetry and bug fix reproductions.

2) Training opt-out: Two options to propose to Navitas counsel — pick one.
  a) Conservative (Customer-protective): "Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs for training, improving, or developing models or model weights for Redwood's general-purpose models, except as expressly authorized in writing. Redwood may process Customer Content to provide the Services and to comply with Safety, security, and abuse prevention obligations."
  b) Operational compromise (standard): "Customer may elect to opt-out of Redwood's use of Customer Content for model training by selecting an explicit setting in the Service or by written notice. If Customer does not elect the opt-out, Redwood may use Customer Content in aggregated and anonymized form to improve and maintain the Service."

3) Telemetry & retention: Proposed snippet: "Redwood collects usage telemetry strictly for service operation, security, and model performance. Redwood will not expose raw Customer Content to third parties for model training. Telemetry retention period is 90 days by default; extended retention is available under a separate agreement. Any telemetry used to improve models will be aggregated and de-identified."

Attachments: marked-up Redlines_MSA_LegalComments.docx (high-level comments + exact snippets).

If Navitas prefers the conservative opt-out, we will need to route to product/infra for an implementation and pricing delta. If they pick the operational compromise, we can accept as standard with self-serve opt-out flag.

—Laura

Alex — quick operational note from CS after legal's suggestions. Two practical constraints we should call out to Navitas so expectations are aligned:

- Endpoint carveouts: If you want an opt-out that applies only to specific endpoints (e.g., analytics-enrichment endpoint used by internal workflows), we can support that, but it'll require scoping the endpoints and adding a per-endpoint flag in prod. That work typically adds ~4-6 weeks to onboarding and is billable as setup.

- Telemetry for safety: We must retain some minimal telemetry (non-content traces, hashed prompts, error logs) for 90 days to investigate abuse and outages. Complete removal of logs impacts debugging and SLA triage. We can offer extended retention controls in Dedicated or Private deployments.

Suggested next step: Alex, do you want (1) the conservative legal language and a pricing/implementation estimate from Product/Ops, or (2) the operational compromise (opt-out toggle) that we can enable immediately in Hosted with a policy note? If you want (1), I'll scope the effort and pull in Product.

Thanks — Monica

Thanks, team — that helps a lot. Navitas Legal prefers the conservative language (2a) for the training opt-out, but we understand there may be a pricing or implementation impact. Our preference is: ownership assigned to Navitas (as per your snippet) and a clear written opt-out that requires Redwood to not use Customer Content for training. Can you send a redlined Order Form / MSA back to us with the conservative language and an estimate for any onboarding/programming work? If we can get an estimate, Navitas Procurement can fast-track a P.O.

Also please include a short statement on telemetry retention (we prefer 30 days, but will consider 90 if needed for safety reasons).

If you can send the redline and the DocuSign-ready Order Form link, we'll start internal approvals.
